verdict.summary: Two different stories. Sign-in and posting as the member are self-serve and work the same day, once a LinkedIn Page super admin verifies your app. Almost everything else (ads, company pages, Sales Navigator, recruiting) needs partner approval with no published timeline.

time_to_first_connection.estimate: 30 minutes (if you control a Page) to days (if you need someone else's approval)
time_to_first_connection.basis: Credentials are issued at app creation, but the app must be associated with a LinkedIn Page and verified by its super admin, who has 30 days to approve.

time_to_production.estimate: Same day (self-serve products) · weeks to never (partner programs)
time_to_production.basis: LinkedIn says most permissions require explicit approval; partner access is decided per applicant. No timelines published.

top_blockers: Every app needs a LinkedIn Page and super-admin verification
Marketing, Sales and Talent APIs are partner programs with no guaranteed approval
Self-serve apps reportedly can't use programmatic refresh tokens

key_decision.question: Can your use case live inside the self-serve products?
key_decision.recommendation: If you only need sign-in (openid, profile, email) and posting as the member (w_member_social), stay self-serve. If you need company pages, ads or lead data, apply to the partner program early and plan a fallback.
key_decision.why: Self-serve products are available immediately; partner programs are approved case by case.

prerequisites.item: LinkedIn account and developer portal access
A LinkedIn Company Page, and its super admin's cooperation
Privacy policy URL and square logo

steps.title: Create the app and pick its LinkedIn Page
steps.detail: The Page's company becomes the app's publisher. Third-party guides say this can't be changed later.

steps.title: Generate the super-admin verification request
steps.detail: Write the message that sends the Page verification URL to your LinkedIn Page super admin and explains what they are approving.

steps.title: Send the Page verification URL to the super admin
steps.detail: Settings → Verify → Generate URL. The super admin has 30 days to approve; a denial invalidates all generated links.

steps.title: Map features to self-serve vs partner permissions
steps.detail: Sort each feature into what the self-serve products cover (sign-in, posting as the member) and what needs a partner program (company pages, ads, lead data).

steps.title: Add self-serve products
steps.detail: Products tab: 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn'. Add redirect URLs on the Auth tab.

steps.title: Apply for partner programs if needed
steps.detail: Marketing (Advertising API) is applied for in the Developer Portal; Sales Navigator via SNAP; Talent via partner applications. Some programs are closed.

steps.title: LinkedIn decides
steps.detail: Approval depends on use case, data needed and volume.

nuances.title: Users must re-consent when tokens expire
nuances.detail: Third-party sources say programmatic refresh tokens are limited to approved partners, so self-serve apps send users back through the OAuth screen.

nuances.title: Development tier is not production
nuances.detail: Third-party sources say Marketing access starts at a limited Development tier, and Standard tier needs a separate review with a video.

blockers.fix: Identify the super admin first and resend the link; links last 30 days.

blockers.symptom: Needed permission isn't available to request
blockers.cause: It belongs to a partner program
blockers.fix: Apply through the Developer Portal or redesign around self-serve products.

agent_can: Map your features to self-serve vs partner permissions
Draft the partner application use-case description
Generate the super-admin verification request message
you_must: Create the app signed in to LinkedIn
Get the Page super admin to approve
Submit partner applications and any review video

unverified: Refresh-token restriction comes from third parties, not LinkedIn docs checked today.
Partner approval timelines are not published.
Whether the associated Page can be changed after creation.
